nodes.summary: Given an input list of symbols with natural-number weights, a Huffman tree is admissible for the input when its list of weighted leaves, read from left to right, is a permutation of the input list: the leaves of the tree carry exactly the input's (symbol, weight) pairs, with the same multiplicities.
nodes.title: Admissible Huffman trees

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and $s$ a symbol occurring at a leaf of $T$. Then the codeword lookup of $s$ in $T$ succeeds and returns the codeword of $s$ as a leaf symbol of $T$.
nodes.title: Codeword lookup agrees with the leaf code

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and $s$ a symbol occurring at a leaf of $T$. Then the codeword lookup of $s$ in $T$ succeeds.
nodes.title: Every leaf symbol has a codeword

nodes.summary: For a Huffman tree $T$ and a symbol $s$ occurring at a leaf of $T$, the codeword of $s$ is the word that the codeword lookup of $T$ returns for $s$, or the empty word if the lookup fails.
nodes.title: Codeword of a leaf symbol

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and $a$ a symbol, and write $0$ for the bit false and $1$ for the bit true. If $T$ is a single leaf labelled $s$, the codeword of $a$ is the one-bit word $0$ when $a = s$ and is undefined otherwise. Otherwise the codeword of $a$ records the edges from the root of $T$ to the leftmost leaf labelled $a$, with $0$ for a left edge and $1$ for a right edge; it is undefined when no leaf of $T$ is…
nodes.title: Codeword lookup in a Huffman tree

nodes.summary: For a real number $v$, a weight tree $T$ and a natural number $d$, the relation "$T$ contains $v$ at depth $d$" is defined inductively: the leaf of weight $v$ contains $v$ at depth $0$, and if $L$ contains $v$ at depth $d$ or $R$ contains $v$ at depth $d$, then the fork with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ contains $v$ at depth $d + 1$. Thus it holds exactly when some leaf of $T$ of weight $v$ lies at depth…
nodes.title: Weight at a given depth

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a weight tree, let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers and let $M$ be a multiset of real numbers such that the multiset of leaf weights of $T$ is $\{a, b\} + M$, $a \le b$, and $b \le w$ for every $w \in M$. Then there is a weight tree $T'$ whose multiset of leaf weights is $\{a + b\} + M$ and whose path cost satisfies $\mathrm{cost}(T') + a + b \le \mathrm{cost}(T)$, where $\mathrm{cost}$ denotes path cost.
nodes.title: Contracting the two least weights

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and let $s_1, \dots, s_n$ ($n \ge 0$) be symbols occurring at leaves of $T$, with codewords $c(s_1), \dots, c(s_n)$ as leaf symbols of $T$. Decoding the concatenation $c(s_1) c(s_2) \cdots c(s_n)$ with $T$ succeeds and returns the sequence $s_1, \dots, s_n$.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts the leaf code

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and let $s_1, \dots, s_n$ ($n \ge 0$) be symbols occurring at leaves of $T$. Encoding $s_1, \dots, s_n$ with $T$ and then decoding the resulting bit string with $T$, failing if the encoding fails, returns $s_1, \dots, s_n$. In particular, the encoding succeeds.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts encoding

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and $w$ a bit string, and write $0$ for the bit false and $1$ for the bit true. If $T$ is a single leaf labelled $s$, decoding one codeword from $w$ returns $s$ together with the rest of $w$ when $w$ starts with $0$, and fails otherwise. If $T$ is a fork with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, it fails when $w$ is empty; when $w$ is a bit $b$ followed by $w'$, it follows $w'$ from the…
nodes.title: Decoding one codeword

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and $w$ a bit string, and write $0$ for the bit false and $1$ for the bit true. Following $w$ in $T$ starts at the root and reads the bits of $w$ one at a time, moving to the left subtree on $0$ and to the right subtree on $1$, until it reaches a leaf; it then returns the label of that leaf together with the unread bits of $w$. It fails if $w$ runs out before a leaf is reached. In…
nodes.title: Following a path in a Huffman tree

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree. Decoding the empty bit string with $T$ returns the empty sequence of symbols. To decode a nonempty bit string $w$, decode one codeword from $w$ with $T$, obtaining a symbol $s$ and the unread bits $w'$, and return $s$ followed by the decoding of $w'$; decoding fails if decoding one codeword from $w$ fails or if decoding $w'$ fails.
nodes.title: Decoding a bit string

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree and let $s_1, \dots, s_n$ ($n \ge 0$) be symbols occurring at leaves of $T$, with codewords $c(s_1), \dots, c(s_n)$ as leaf symbols of $T$. Encoding $s_1, \dots, s_n$ with $T$ succeeds and returns the concatenation $c(s_1) c(s_2) \cdots c(s_n)$.
nodes.title: Encoding concatenates leaf codewords

nodes.summary: Given a coding tree $T$, the empty message encodes to the empty bit string, and a message $s_1 s_2 \cdots s_n$ encodes to the concatenation, in order, of the codewords of $s_1, \dots, s_n$ in $T$. If some $s_i$ has no codeword in $T$, the message has no encoding.
nodes.title: Huffman encoding of a message

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a coding tree whose leaf symbols are pairwise distinct. For a symbol $s$, let $\ell(s)$ be the length of the codeword of $s$ in $T$, or $0$ if $s$ has no codeword. Then the encoded length of $T$ equals $\sum_{(s, w)} w \cdot \ell(s)$, the sum over the weighted leaves $(s, w)$ of $T$.
nodes.title: Encoded length is the total weighted codeword length

nodes.summary: For any two coding trees $L$ and $R$, the encoded length of the tree with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ equals its weighted path length.
nodes.title: Encoded length of a fork

nodes.summary: The encoded length of a leaf of weight $w$ is $w$ (its lone symbol receives a one-bit codeword). The encoded length of the tree with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ is $P(L) + P(R) + W(L) + W(R)$, where $P$ is the weighted path length and $W$ the total weight; this is the weighted path length of that tree.
nodes.title: Encoded length of a coding tree

nodes.summary: For every Huffman tree $T$, the path cost of the weight tree obtained from $T$ by erasing its symbols equals the weighted path length of $T$, viewed as a real number.
nodes.title: Erasing symbols preserves weighted path length

nodes.summary: For every Huffman tree $T$, the total weight of the weight tree obtained from $T$ by erasing its symbols equals the total weight of $T$, viewed as a real number.
nodes.title: Erasing symbols preserves total weight

nodes.summary: For every Huffman tree $T$, the multiset of leaf weights of the weight tree obtained from $T$ by erasing its symbols is the multiset of the weights $w$, viewed as real numbers, over the weighted leaves $(s, w)$ of $T$.
nodes.title: Erasing symbols preserves leaf weights

nodes.summary: Erasing the symbols of a Huffman tree gives the weight tree of the same shape: a leaf with symbol $s$ and natural-number weight $w$ becomes the leaf of real weight $w$, and a fork with subtrees $L$ and $R$ becomes the fork whose subtrees are the erasures of $L$ and $R$.
nodes.title: Erasing symbols from a Huffman tree

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a weight tree of height $h \ge 1$. Then there are real numbers $x$ and $y$, a multiset $M$ of real numbers and a real number $c$ such that the multiset of leaf weights of $T$ is $\{x, y\} + M$, the path cost of $T$ is $c + hx + hy$, and for every real number $z$ there is a weight tree $T'$ of height at most $h$ whose multiset of leaf weights is $\{z\} + M$ and whose path cost is $c + (h - 1)z$.
nodes.title: Contracting a deepest sibling pair

nodes.summary: If extracting two minima from a binary min-heap $h$ of Huffman priorities succeeds with first priority $p_1$, second priority $p_2$ and remaining heap $h'$, then the multiset of elements of $h$ equals the multiset of elements of $h'$ with $p_1$ and $p_2$ added, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Extracting two minima preserves the heap's elements

nodes.summary: Order Huffman priorities lexicographically by weight and then serial number. If extracting two minima from a binary min-heap $h$ of Huffman priorities succeeds with first priority $p_1$, second priority $p_2$ and remaining heap $h'$, then $p_1 \le q$ for every element $q$ of $h$, and $p_2 \le q$ for every $q$ that is $p_2$ or an element of $h'$.
nodes.title: Two-minimum extraction is greedy

nodes.summary: Given a binary min-heap $h$ of Huffman priorities, extract the minimum of $h$, obtaining a priority $p_1$ and a heap $h_1$, then extract the minimum of $h_1$, obtaining a priority $p_2$ and a heap $h_2$. The result is the triple $(p_1, p_2, h_2)$; if either extraction meets an empty heap, there is no result.
nodes.title: Extracting two minima from a Huffman heap

nodes.summary: The height of a weight tree is the number of edges on a longest path from the root to a leaf: a leaf has height $0$, and a fork with subtrees $L$ and $R$ has height $1 + \max(\mathrm{height}(L), \mathrm{height}(R))$.
nodes.title: Height of a weight tree

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of symbol–weight pairs with natural-number weights, over a symbol type with decidable equality, and suppose Huffman's algorithm returns the tree $t$ on $L$. Then every Huffman tree $t'$ that is admissible for $L$, that is, whose weighted leaves listed from left to right form a permutation of $L$, has encoded length at least that of $t$.
nodes.title: Huffman's algorithm minimizes the encoded length

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of symbol–weight pairs with natural-number weights, over a symbol type with decidable equality. The Huffman construction returns no tree on $L$ if and only if $L$ is empty or some symbol occurs in $L$ more than once.
nodes.title: Huffman's construction fails exactly on empty or repeated-symbol inputs

nodes.summary: The cost of a list of Huffman work items is the real number obtained by summing, over the items in the list, the weighted path length of each item's tree.
nodes.title: Cost of a Huffman work forest

nodes.summary: The weighted leaves of a list of Huffman work items are the concatenation, in list order, of the weighted leaves of the items' trees.
nodes.title: Weighted leaves of a Huffman work forest

nodes.summary: The priorities of a list of Huffman work items form the multiset consisting of the priority of each item in the list, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Priorities of a Huffman work forest

nodes.summary: The weights of a list of Huffman work items form the multiset consisting of the total leaf weight of each item's tree, taken as a real number, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Weights of a Huffman work forest

nodes.summary: The heap of a list of Huffman work items is obtained from the empty binary min-heap by inserting the priorities of the items one at a time, in list order.
nodes.title: Heap of a Huffman work forest

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a nonempty list of symbol–weight pairs with natural-number weights, over a symbol type with decidable equality. If no symbol occurs in $L$ more than once, then the Huffman construction returns a tree on $L$.
nodes.title: Huffman's construction succeeds on nonempty inputs with distinct symbols

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $H$ a binary min-heap of Huffman priorities and $T$ an array of optional Huffman work items, and let $F$ be the list of work items stored in $T$, in array order. The invariant holds when the multiset of elements of $H$ equals the multiset of priorities of the items of $F$; the serial numbers of the items of $F$ are pairwise distinct; every item of $F$ has serial number less than $n$;…
nodes.title: Huffman loop invariant

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a merge budget, $n$ a next serial number, $h$ a binary min-heap of Huffman priorities and $t$ a serial-indexed table of optional Huffman work items. If the Huffman loop with budget $k$ on $n$, $h$ and $t$ returns a tree $T$, then the Huffman loop with lookup counting on the same arguments returns $T$ together with the count $2k + 1$ of indexed payload-table reads.
nodes.title: Indexed reads of a successful Huffman loop

nodes.summary: The loop takes a fuel $n$, a next serial number $s$, a binary min-heap $H$ of Huffman priorities, ordered lexicographically by weight and then serial number, a table $T$ whose cells each hold at most one work item, and a counter $c$. Taking serial $i$ from a table succeeds when cell $i$ holds a work item whose priority has serial number $i$, and returns that item's tree together with the table with cell $i$…
nodes.title: Huffman loop with an accumulated lookup count

nodes.summary: For every fuel $n$, next serial number $s$, binary min-heap $H$ of Huffman priorities and table $T$ whose cells each hold at most one work item, the Huffman loop with lookup count on $(n, s, H, T)$ fails exactly when the bounded Huffman merge loop on $(n, s, H, T)$ fails, and returns $(t, 2n + 1)$ when the merge loop returns the tree $t$: two indexed table reads for each of the $n$ merges and one for the final step.
nodes.title: Lookup count of the instrumented Huffman loop

nodes.summary: For every fuel $n$, next serial number $s$, binary min-heap $H$ of Huffman priorities and table $T$ whose cells each hold at most one work item, discarding the count from the result of the Huffman loop with lookup count on $(n, s, H, T)$ gives the result of the bounded Huffman merge loop on $(n, s, H, T)$: the two fail together, and otherwise they return the same tree.
nodes.title: Discarding the lookup count recovers the Huffman loop

nodes.summary: For a fuel $n$, a next serial number $s$, a binary min-heap $H$ of Huffman priorities and a table $T$ whose cells each hold at most one work item, the Huffman loop with lookup count on $(n, s, H, T)$ is the Huffman loop with an accumulated lookup count on $(n, s, H, T)$ started with counter $0$. It runs the bounded sequence of Huffman merges and counts indexed table lookups, one for each work item taken from the…
nodes.title: Huffman loop with lookup count

nodes.summary: The loop takes a fuel $n$, a next serial number $s$, a binary min-heap $H$ of Huffman priorities, ordered lexicographically by weight and then serial number, and a table $T$ whose cells each hold at most one work item. Taking serial $i$ from a table succeeds when cell $i$ holds a work item whose priority has serial number $i$, and returns that item's tree together with the table with cell $i$ emptied. With fuel…
nodes.title: Bounded Huffman merge loop

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of symbol–weight pairs with natural-number weights, over a symbol type with decidable equality, and suppose the Huffman construction returns the tree $t$ on $L$. Then the weighted path length of $t$, as a real number, is the cost of a two-minimum merge trace for the multiset of the weights of $L$, taken as reals: starting from that multiset, repeatedly replace two weights $x \le y$ such that every…
nodes.title: Huffman's construction follows a two-minimum merge trace

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of symbol–weight pairs with natural-number weights, and let $t$ and $t'$ be coding trees with symbols of the same type. Suppose the weighted path length of $t$, as a real number, is the cost of a two-minimum merge trace for the multiset of the weights of $L$, taken as reals (repeatedly replace two weights $x \le y$, with every other weight at least $y$, by $x + y$ until one weight remains, the…
nodes.title: A two-minimum merge trace gives a minimum weighted path length

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of symbol–weight pairs with natural-number weights, over a symbol type with decidable equality, and suppose the Huffman construction returns the tree $t$ on $L$. Then every coding tree $t'$ (a full binary tree whose leaves carry symbols and weights) whose weighted leaves, listed left to right, form a permutation of $L$ has weighted path length at least that of $t$.
nodes.title: Optimality of Huffman coding

nodes.summary: If the Huffman construction succeeds on a list of weighted symbols and returns a tree $T$, then the code of $T$ on its leaf symbols is prefix-free: for any two distinct leaf symbols of $T$, neither codeword is a prefix of the other.
nodes.title: Huffman codes are prefix-free

nodes.summary: A Huffman priority is a pair $(w, s)$ of natural numbers: a weight $w$ and a serial number $s$.
nodes.title: Huffman priority

nodes.summary: For every list of weighted symbols, the work forest read off the initial serial-indexed table of the list is exactly the initial leaf forest of the list, in the same order.
nodes.title: The initial table holds the initial forest

nodes.summary: For every table $T$ whose cells each hold at most one work item and every work item $x$, the work forest of the table obtained from $T$ by appending a new last cell holding $x$ is the work forest of $T$ followed by $x$.
nodes.title: Appending to the table appends to the forest

nodes.summary: For a table $T$ whose cells each hold at most one work item, the work forest of $T$ is the list of the work items held in the cells of $T$, in increasing cell order; empty cells are skipped.
nodes.title: Work forest of a table

nodes.summary: A Huffman tree over an alphabet $\alpha$ is either a leaf, which carries a symbol $a \in \alpha$ and a natural-number weight $w$, or a fork, which joins a left and a right Huffman tree over $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Huffman tree

nodes.summary: A record consisting of two Huffman priorities, the first and the second, together with a binary min-heap of Huffman priorities, the rest.
nodes.title: Result of a two-minimum extraction

nodes.summary: A Huffman weight tree is a full binary tree whose leaves carry only real weights: it is either a leaf with a weight $w \in \mathbb{R}$, or a fork joining a left and a right Huffman weight tree.
nodes.title: Huffman weight tree

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of pairs $(a, w)$ of a symbol $a$ and a natural-number weight $w$, with decidable equality on symbols. If the Huffman construction on $L$ succeeds with a tree $T$, then the list of weighted leaves of $T$, read left to right, is a permutation of $L$.
nodes.title: Huffman's construction keeps the weighted leaves

nodes.summary: A work item over an alphabet $\alpha$ pairs a Huffman priority, that is, a natural-number weight and a natural-number serial, with a Huffman tree over $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Huffman work item

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of $n$ pairs $(a_0, w_0), \dots, (a_{n-1}, w_{n-1})$ of symbols and natural-number weights, with decidable equality on symbols. The construction fails when $L$ is empty or two pairs share a symbol. Otherwise it starts from $n$ leaves, the leaf for $(a_i, w_i)$ having priority (weight $w_i$, serial $i$), and performs $n - 1$ merges: each merge removes the two trees whose priorities are least in the…
nodes.title: Huffman's algorithm

nodes.summary: Given a starting serial number $s$ and a list of pairs $(a_0, w_0), \dots, (a_{k-1}, w_{k-1})$ of symbols and natural-number weights, this is the list of $k$ Huffman work items whose $i$-th entry has priority (weight $w_i$, serial $s + i$) and whose tree is the leaf with symbol $a_i$ and weight $w_i$.
nodes.title: Numbered leaf work items

nodes.summary: For a list of pairs $(a_0, w_0), \dots, (a_{k-1}, w_{k-1})$ of symbols and natural-number weights, the initial forest is the list of $k$ Huffman work items whose $i$-th entry has priority (weight $w_i$, serial $i$) and whose tree is the leaf with symbol $a_i$ and weight $w_i$.
nodes.title: Initial Huffman forest

nodes.summary: For a list of $k$ pairs $(a_0, w_0), \dots, (a_{k-1}, w_{k-1})$ of symbols and natural-number weights, the initial table is the array of length $k$ of optional Huffman work items whose cell $i$ is present and holds the work item with priority (weight $w_i$, serial $i$) and tree the leaf with symbol $a_i$ and weight $w_i$; that is, it is the initial Huffman forest with every entry marked present.
nodes.title: Initial Huffman table

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a multiset of real weights and let $c$ be a merge cost of $W$ certified by a two-minimum merge trace. Then every Huffman weight tree whose multiset of leaf weights is $W$ has weighted external path length at least $c$.
nodes.title: Two-minimum merge costs lower-bound weighted path length

nodes.summary: For a Huffman tree $T$ over an alphabet $\alpha$, the type of leaf symbols of $T$ is the subtype of those $a \in \alpha$ that occur in the list of leaf symbols of $T$.
nodes.title: Type of leaf symbols of a Huffman tree

nodes.summary: The relation "$c$ is a two-minimum merge cost of the multiset $W$ of real weights" is defined inductively by two rules. A singleton multiset $\{w\}$ has merge cost $0$. If $a \le b$, every element of the multiset $R$ is at least $b$, and $c$ is a merge cost of $\{a + b\} + R$, then $a + b + c$ is a merge cost of $\{a, b\} + R$. Thus a merge cost is the total cost of repeatedly replacing two smallest weights by…
nodes.title: Two-minimum merge trace

nodes.summary: For a Huffman tree $T$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a symbol $a \in \alpha$, the root-to-leaf path code of $a$ in $T$ is undefined exactly when $a$ is not among the leaf symbols of $T$.
nodes.title: A symbol has a path code exactly when it labels a leaf

nodes.summary: For a Huffman tree $T$ and a symbol $s$, the path code of $s$ in $T$ records the edges on the path from the root of $T$ to the leftmost leaf labelled $s$, writing false for a left edge and true for a right edge. If $T$ is a single leaf labelled $s$, the path code is empty; if no leaf of $T$ is labelled $s$, there is no path code.
nodes.title: Root-to-leaf path code

nodes.summary: For a Huffman weight tree $T$, write $w(T)$ for its total leaf weight. The weighted external path length $P(T)$ of $T$ is defined by the merge recurrence: a leaf $T$ has $P(T) = 0$, and a tree $T$ with subtrees $L$ and $R$ has $P(T) = P(L) + P(R) + w(L) + w(R)$.
nodes.title: Weighted external path length of a Huffman weight tree

nodes.summary: For every Huffman tree $T$, the codeword map on the symbols occurring as leaves of $T$ is prefix-free: if $a$ and $b$ are distinct leaf symbols of $T$, then the codeword of $a$ is not a prefix of the codeword of $b$.
nodes.title: Huffman tree codes are prefix-free

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman weight tree whose height is at most a natural number $B$, and write $W(T)$ for its multiset of leaf weights. Let $v \le r$ be real numbers and let $S$ be a multiset of reals with $\{r\} + W(T) = \{v\} + S$. Then there is a Huffman weight tree $T'$ with multiset of leaf weights $S$ and height at most $B$ whose weighted external path length is at most that of $T$ plus $B(r - v)$.
nodes.title: Raising one leaf weight in a bounded-height tree

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman weight tree whose height is at most a natural number $B$, and write $W(T)$ for its multiset of leaf weights. Let $f, s, \ell, n$ be real numbers with $\ell \le n$, $\ell \le f$ and $n \le s$, and let $S$ be a multiset of reals with $\{f, s\} + W(T) = \{\ell, n\} + S$. Then there is a Huffman weight tree $T'$ with multiset of leaf weights $S$ whose weighted external path length is at most that…
nodes.title: Raising two leaf weights in a bounded-height tree

nodes.summary: Suppose a leaf of weight $v$ occurs at depth $d$ in a Huffman weight tree $T$, and let $r$ be a real number. Then there are a multiset $R$ of reals and a Huffman weight tree $T'$ such that the multiset of leaf weights of $T$ is $\{v\} + R$, that of $T'$ is $\{r\} + R$, the total leaf weight of $T'$ is that of $T$ plus $r - v$, the weighted external path length of $T'$ is that of $T$ plus $d(r - v)$, and $T'$ has…
nodes.title: Reweighting one leaf occurrence

nodes.summary: The list of the symbols at the leaves of a Huffman tree, read from left to right, with one entry per leaf.
nodes.title: List of leaf symbols of a Huffman tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a table of optional Huffman work items. If removing serial number $s$ from $t$ succeeds and returns a tree together with an updated table $t'$, then for every index $j \ne s$ the entry of $t'$ at $j$ equals the entry of $t$ at $j$ (both are absent when $j$ is out of bounds).
nodes.title: Removing a serial leaves the other table entries unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a table of optional Huffman work items and let $w$ be a work item with serial number $s$. If the entry of $t$ at index $s$ is $w$, then removing serial $s$ from $t$ succeeds and returns the tree of $w$ together with an updated table.
nodes.title: A stored work item can be removed by its serial

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a table of optional Huffman work items, and call the list of work items present in a table its work forest. If removing serial number $s$ from $t$ succeeds and returns a tree $T$ and an updated table $t'$, then there is a work item $w$ with tree $T$ and serial number $s$ such that $w$ followed by the work forest of $t'$ is a permutation of the work forest of $t$.
nodes.title: Removing a serial removes one work item from the forest

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a table of optional Huffman work items. If removing serial number $s$ from $t$ succeeds and returns a tree together with an updated table $t'$, then $t'$ has the same size as $t$.
nodes.title: Removing a serial preserves the table size

nodes.summary: Given a serial number $s$ and a table $t$ of optional Huffman work items, look up the entry of $t$ at index $s$. If that entry is a work item whose serial number is $s$, the result is its tree together with the table obtained from $t$ by emptying the entry at $s$; otherwise (the index is out of bounds, the entry is empty, or it holds an item with a different serial number) the removal fails.
nodes.title: Removing a work item by serial

nodes.summary: The total weight of a Huffman weight tree is the sum of its leaf weights: a leaf of weight $w$ has total weight $w$, and a tree with subtrees $L$ and $R$ has total weight equal to the total weight of $L$ plus that of $R$.
nodes.title: Total leaf weight of a Huffman weight tree

nodes.summary: The sum of the weights at all leaves of a Huffman tree, counted once per leaf.
nodes.title: Total weight of a Huffman tree

nodes.summary: The list of pairs $(s, w)$, one for each leaf of a Huffman tree, where $s$ is the symbol and $w$ the weight at that leaf, read from left to right.
nodes.title: Weighted leaves of a Huffman tree

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a Huffman tree whose leaf symbols are pairwise distinct. Then the weighted path length of $T$ equals the sum, over the leaves of $T$ with symbol $s$ and weight $w$, of $w$ times the length of the root-to-leaf path of $s$ in $T$ (the depth of that leaf, with the root at depth zero).
nodes.title: Weighted path length as a sum over leaves

nodes.summary: For Huffman trees $L$ and $R$, the weighted path length of the tree with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ equals the weighted path length of $L$ plus the weighted path length of $R$ plus the total weight of $L$ plus the total weight of $R$.
nodes.title: Weighted path length of a merged tree

nodes.summary: The weighted path length of a Huffman tree is defined recursively: a single leaf has weighted path length $0$, and the tree with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ has weighted path length equal to the weighted path length of $L$ plus that of $R$ plus the total weight of $L$ plus the total weight of $R$.
nodes.title: Weighted path length

nodes.summary: The leaf weights of a Huffman weight tree form a multiset of reals that forgets where the leaves sit: a leaf of weight $w$ gives $\{w\}$, and a tree with subtrees $L$ and $R$ gives the multiset sum of the leaf weights of $L$ and those of $R$.
nodes.title: Multiset of leaf weights

fully_proved.label: fully proved
